title: Charge Tunable Optical Nonlinearity of Moiré Exciton-Polaritons
authors: Zhijie Li, Kok Wee Song, Jens-Christian Drawer, Vita Solovyeva, Martin Esmann, Niklas Nilius, Muhammad Sufyan Ramzan, Caterina Cocchi, Falk Eilenberger, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Atanu Patra, Subhamoy Sahoo, Simon Betzold, Sven Höfling, Alexander Högele, Oleksandr Kyriienko, Christian Schneider, Bo Han
abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenides represent a versatile platform to study strong light-matter interactions based on excitons and electrons in ordered lattices. Twist-engineering of moiré structures further enables the manipulation of the polaritonic nonlinearities via engineering the exciton landscape on the nanoscale. In this work, we demonstrate in-situ control of the optical saturation-based nonlinearity of moiré exciton-polaritons by phase space restriction via charge doping. Strong exciton-photon coupling is established in a gate-controllable MoTe$_2$-MoSe$_2$ heterobilayer, embedded in a spectrally-tunable open cavity. A small gate voltage can effectively lower the necessary polariton density by one order of magnitude to achieve a similar nonlinear saturation effect as in the charge-neutral case. Our microscopic description successfully explains the observed phenomena in the framework of Pauli blocking for the moiré superlattices with charge preoccupation.
summary: The authors demonstrate electrical control over the nonlinear optical response of moiré exciton-polaritons using a gated $	ext{MoTe}_2-	ext{MoSe}_2$ heterobilayer. By inducing charge doping, they show that the required excitation density to reach saturation can be drastically lowered compared to neutral conditions. This work combines advanced cavity QED experiments with microscopic theory rooted in Pauli blocking.
main_problem: The study focuses on demonstrating and understanding the *in-situ* electrical control of optical saturation-based nonlinearity in moiré exciton-polaritons.
main_result: A small gate voltage can significantly reduce the required polariton density by an order of magnitude to achieve a comparable nonlinear saturation effect compared to charge-neutral conditions.
method: The research combines experimental measurements (PL, DR) on a gated heterobilayer with microscopic theoretical modeling based on Pauli blocking for moiré superlattices.
model_or_system: The physical system is a gate-controllable $	ext{MoTe}_2-	ext{MoSe}_2$ heterobilayer embedded in an open optical microcavity, forming moiré exciton-polaritons. The theory incorporates charge doping effects via Pauli blocking mechanisms.
key_observables: Gate voltage ($V_G$) dependent photoluminescence (PL), differential reflectivity (DR) showing anti-crossings and saturation behavior, Rabi splittings, and excitonic Stokes shifts.
important_parameters: Moiré superlattice constant $a_M \approx 4.2 	ext{ nm}$, gate voltage regimes (hole/electron doping), and the required polariton density for saturation ($	ext{dex-pol}$).
main_assumptions: The theoretical description successfully explains observations within the framework of Pauli blocking applied to moiré superlattices with charge occupancy.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematics of the cavity/HBL, PL/DR spectra showing gate tunability and anti-crossings, and density-dependent DR curves demonstrating Rabi gap saturation effects.
paper_structure: The paper builds context by reviewing related literature (citations) before presenting experimental results on charge tuning ($	ext{PL}$/$	ext{DR}$) and then using theory to explain the observed nonlinear saturation phenomena via Pauli blocking.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses open quantum systems dynamics, specifically cavity QED effects in solid-state materials. The ability to electrically tune nonlinearity via doping provides a powerful platform for studying many-body interactions in engineered quantum optical systems.
